The FFI Bridge and Host Interop

This page explains how vm bridges @extern calls in SA assembly, built-in functions invoked via call @fn, and references to host plugin symbols, down to the libffi / POSIX dlopen / Windows LoadLibraryExW layer. After reading this section you will understand how the sap.json dependency block takes effect, what --allow-ffi actually opens, where the policy engine intercepts on the dispatch path, and the full list of shims built into vm.

Three Interop Channels

ChannelSA-side spellingvm-side implementationTypical representatives
Typed FFI@extern fd_open(path: ptr) -> i32 + call @fd_open(&PATH)src/ffi.zig::callSymbolWithPtr calls in via libffiAll @extern declarations
Raw libc FFI@extern dlopen(...)Only when --allow-ffi is given does resolveSymbol return these symbolsdlopen / dlsym / dlclose / dlerror
Built-in shimDirectly call @fd_open(...) (also possible without @extern)At parse time the name is mapped to a pub export fn built into vmfd_* / mmap / signal / pthread_* / sqlite3_* / sa_time_*

Typed FFI: The libffi Bridge

Each @extern is folded at parse time into a parser.ExternSignature, structured as “return type + parameter type array”. When vm executes call @fn, it packs the values in the guest registers according to the signature into the FfiValue extern union (source src/ffi.zig::writeArgValue), then goes through libffi with ffi_prep_cif + ffi_call.

Supported parameter types: void / i1 / u8 / i8 / u16 / i16 / u32 / i32 / u64 / i64 / f32 / f64 / ptr. Pointers and integers have the same width on 64-bit platforms; i32 is sign-extended, u32 is zero-extended.

libffi on Windows

On Windows, libffi is not in a system DLL. On the first callSymbolWithPtr, vm tries to LoadLibrary + GetProcAddress in the order libffi-8.dll → libffi-7.dll → ffi.dll, resolving all ffi_type_* statics. On failure it returns error.WindowsLibffiUnavailable.

Raw libc FFI: --allow-ffi

POSIX dlopen, dlsym, dlclose, dlerror are wrapped in vm as platform-independent function pointers via pub const (Linux / macOS go through @cImport, Windows goes through LoadLibraryExW / FreeLibrary). They are only returned by resolveSymbol when FfiManager.allow_ffi = true —

if (std.mem.eql(u8, symbol_name, "dlopen")) return if (self.allow_ffi) ... else null;
if (std.mem.eql(u8, symbol_name, "dlsym"))  return if (self.allow_ffi) ... else null;
if (std.mem.eql(u8, symbol_name, "dlclose")) return if (self.allow_ffi) ... else null;
if (std.mem.eql(u8, symbol_name, "dlerror")) return if (self.allow_ffi) ... else null;

That is to say:

  • Without --allow-ffi: even if the guest declares @extern dlopen, it gets null at the symbol resolution stage, ending in Symbol not found.
  • With --allow-ffi: the 4 symbols above can be called directly, but capabilities are still further tightened by extern.allow / fs / http etc. in sa.vm.policy/1.

Plugin Dependency Loading (sap.json)

FfiManager.loadDeclaredDependencies does not scan SA_PLUGINS_PATH, but reads $SA_PLUGINS_HOME/installed/vm/current/sap.json (Windows default C:/Users/Public/.sa_plugins, Linux default $HOME/.local/share/sa_plugins), and obtains all dependency names (in sap.json order) from the dependencies section.

Afterwards, the first time resolveSymbol needs a given dependency, loadInstalledPlugin uses {plugins_home}/installed/{name}/current/lib{name}.so (on Windows {name}.dll) via dlopen(..., RTLD_NOW=2); on success the handle is added to the handles list, and subsequent dlsym lookups go directly on the new handle.

In sap.json, vm pins 4 optional dependencies:

nameVersionSymbol countRole
http-client>=0.1.014Synchronous HTTP client bridge
http-server>=0.1.019Synchronous HTTP server bridge
deno>=0.1.01sa_deno_plugin_hostname
node>=0.1.07os.cpus / timers.sleep / dgram.*

If a dependency is not installed, a failed dlopen is printed to stderr, but vm does not terminate because of it — it is the soft error “Declared FFI dependency not loaded”, and other symbols that do not depend on that plugin can still be resolved.

Built-in Shim List

The following symbols are forcibly mapped in src/ffi.zig::resolveSymbol to pub export fn functions built into vm, without depending on any .so / .dll:

FamilySymbolsImplementation
fdfd_open, fd_read, fd_closeCurrently placeholders (fd_open always returns 3, fd_read always returns 3, fd_close always returns 0), for compatibility with existing demos
mmapmmap, munmapmmap uses std.heap.page_allocator.alloc; munmap is a placeholder returning 0
signalsignalPlaceholder: returns the original sig
pthreadpthread_spawn, pthread_spawn_detached, pthread_join, pthread_dropPlaceholders: the s-series returns 0, pthread_drop is a no-op
sqlite3sqlite3_prepare, sqlite3_step, sqlite3_finalizePlaceholders: prepare/finalize return 0, step always returns 100 (SQLITE_DONE)
sa_timesa_time_sleep_ms, sa_time_sleep_nsReal implementation: std.time.sleep
Warningfd_* / mmap / signal / pthread_* / sqlite3_* are currently placeholder implementations, only intended to let existing demos / standard library facades run on vm; do not treat them as real OS behavior. For the production path, use sa build-exe.

Policy Engine Interception on the FFI Path

The capability policy (src/policy.zig, schema sa.vm.policy/1), with the assistance of src/io_classify.zig, performs two layers of checks on each call @fn:

Layer 1: The extern.allow Name Allowlist

Default-deny. The name of the extern symbol being called must be in the policy’s extern.allow list, otherwise extern_not_allowed is thrown, and this happens before libffi / dlopen resolution. This means: when the policy denies, no target file / handle loading error information is leaked — the caller only sees “NAME denied by run policy”.

Layer 2: fs / http / env / process Argument Routing

Via io_classify, each known symbol family is mapped to the corresponding policy check:

Symbol familyPolicy sectionCheck function
fd_*, sa_print_bytes, sa_fmt_*fspolicy.checkFs
sa_http_client_*, sa_http_server_*httppolicy.checkHttp
env read / writeenvpolicy.checkEnv
process spawn / execprocesspolicy.checkProcessSpawn

Each deny is reported in the form of E_CAPABILITY_DENIED (panic code 100, exit code 228), and gives a readable DenyReason.label() in the detail of sa-vm-event: {...} (fs_not_allowed, host_not_allowed, extern_not_allowed, etc.). The source location on the deny path and the concrete target (such as an out-of-bounds URL) are also embedded in the event.

Capability Boundary Quick Reference

  • Enforced: the extern.allow name allowlist, fs.read/write subtree matching (glob + Windows realpath), http domain / method / path / port / IP literal / private address / redirect count / downgrade interception, the env list, the process spawn and exec allowlists, the master switches for ffi / threads / net_raw.
  • Not enforced: redirects spontaneously performed inside native plugins (not at a vm dispatch point), the check-to-use TOCTOU window inside a single shim call.
  • Symbol family classification: see src/io_classify.zig. Symbols not in the classification only go through the Layer 1 check.
NoteThe relationship between the policy and the --sandboxed built-in profile: --sandboxed is equivalent to forcing a default-deny policy (resource caps + a minimal extern set), and cannot be used together with --policy or --allow-ffi — a conflict triggers E_SANDBOX_MISCONFIG, exit code 234.
